title: Optimization Council
field: cross-team optimization council convened and led by Dimitris Bertsimas (MIT): operations research and optimization across linear, integer and mixed-integer, robust and adaptive, convex/conic/moment, stochastic and dynamic, and data-driven optimization, machine learning and statistics under a modern optimization lens, and analytics applications. His research-craft skill is partitioned by optimization domain (the codes in team.json "domains": LO, IO, RO, CP, SD, ML, DA, HS, AP), each domain mapped to the repository teams it engages; research notes and paper cards tag findings with these codes. The council seats the members of the repository's four teams as guest delegations (team.json "guest_teams": LP Team product/lp-team, NLP Team product/nonlinear-team, DFO Team product/dfo-team, MINLP Team product/minlp-team), and Bertsimas convenes and leads their cross-team discussion. Not represented as voices of their own: stochastic programming as a separate tradition, approximate dynamic programming and reinforcement learning, statistical learning theory, and constraint programming

domains.name: Linear optimization
domains.scope: LP theory and geometry, simplex and interior-point methods, network flows, duality as a modelling and proof device

domains.name: Integer and mixed-integer optimization
domains.scope: formulations and their strength, cutting planes and relaxations, algebraic and geometric methods, approximation algorithms, robust discrete optimization

domains.name: Robust, adaptive and distributionally robust optimization
domains.scope: uncertainty sets and the price of robustness, adaptive and affine policies, data-driven and distributionally robust optimization, robust nonconvex and simulation-based optimization

domains.name: Convex, conic and polynomial optimization
domains.scope: moment problems and optimal probability inequalities, semidefinite and sum-of-squares relaxations, randomized and first-order methods for convex programs

domains.name: Stochastic and dynamic optimization, applied probability and queueing
domains.scope: stochastic networks and scheduling, achievable-region and conservation-law methods, bandits, stochastic and dynamic vehicle routing, large deviations, probabilistic analysis of combinatorial problems

domains.name: Machine learning and statistics under a modern optimization lens
domains.scope: best subset selection and sparse regression, optimal classification and regression trees, sparse PCA and clustering, robust, fair and interpretable models

domains.name: Data-driven decisions and prescriptive analytics
domains.scope: from predictive to prescriptive analytics, prescriptive trees, learning to optimize, online mixed-integer optimization, optimization with learned constraints

domains.name: Heuristic, simulation-based and derivative-free search
domains.scope: simulated annealing and local search, robust optimization of simulation-based and black-box problems

domains.name: Applications as optimization testbeds
domains.scope: air transportation and vehicle routing, finance and execution, revenue management and pricing, healthcare, fairness, operations management

chase_hints: MIT DSpace open-access articles (dspace.mit.edu; MIT faculty open-access policy) and MIT Operations Research Center working papers
SSRN for finance, revenue-management and operations-management papers; medRxiv for COVID-19 era healthcare papers

card_dimensions.D1: problem and entry point: which assumption, gap or application forced the problem and how it is stated; also name the optimization domain(s) of the work with the codes in team.json "domains" (for example RO, or IO+ML)
card_dimensions.D3: model and data: problem class, the uncertainty or data model (uncertainty sets, distributions or moments, samples, real data sets), constraints, and which assumptions are adopted for tractability (as the authors admit)
card_dimensions.D4: formulation and analysis: reformulation devices (duality, conic or mixed-integer reformulations, cutting planes, decomposition), algorithm design, proof skeletons, approximation, complexity or probabilistic bounds; n/a for purely empirical work
card_dimensions.D5: computational and empirical evaluation: instances or data sets (synthetic or real), named baselines and solvers with versions, metrics (optimality gap, out-of-sample performance, runtime, accuracy, interpretability), the scale reached, and whether failures or limits are reported

members.name: Dimitris Bertsimas
members.hint: Boeing Professor of Operations Research, MIT (Sloan School of Management and Operations Research Center); textbooks Introduction to Linear Optimization (with J. N. Tsitsiklis, 1997) and Optimization over Integers (with R. Weismantel, 2005); robust optimization ('The price of robustness', with M. Sim, 2004; 'Theory and applications of robust optimization', 2011), moment problems and semidefinite optimization, simulated annealing (1993), best subset selection via a modern optimization lens (2016), optimal classification trees (2017), from predictive to prescriptive analytics (2020); his homepage files papers under topic folders (robust optimization, machine learning under a modern optimization lens, moment problems, stochastic networks, queueing, finance, air transportation, healthcare and others). Not Dimitri P. Bertsekas (MIT LIDS, dynamic programming), a different person
